steps.content: The idea says a coin sitting near its recent high is strong, so the factor should rise as its recent high relative to its recent low rises. The cleanest cross-coin-comparable measure is the ratio of the recent high to the recent low, which is a unit-free number between 0 and infinity and thus comparable across coins. I'll start with the plainest version over a 5-day window.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0612
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0202 (t = -8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0305, 2023 -0.0164, 2024 -0.0189

The plain high/low ratio comes out clearly negative and consistent across all three periods, so on this history coins sitting near their recent high have actually done worse — the opposite of the idea. Before concluding, I'll check whether the same idea measured differently (where the recent high sits inside the recent range, not the ratio itself) behaves differently, since a ratio can be dominated by a single extreme day.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0182
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0034 (t = -1.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0117, 2023 +0.0035, 2024 -0.0061

The position-inside-its-range version is much weaker and flips sign between periods, so the ratio form is the better reading of "trading near its recent high". One more form of the same idea: where today's close sits inside its own recent range, which is a different way of saying "trading near the high".

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0278
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0074 (t = -3.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0191, 2023 -0.0039, 2024 -0.0051

Three forms of the same idea all come out negative, so the sign is not an artifact of one measurement: the plain 5-day high/low ratio gives −0.0202, the 5-day position-in-range gives −0.0034 (weak and unstable across periods), and the 5-day close-in-range position gives −0.0074. The plain ratio is the strongest and most stable, so I'll hand that in with the sign the idea predicts: near its recent high is bearish on this history, and the factor rises as the ratio rises.

<factor>Factor('high').safe_div(Factor('low')).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea points at a persistent, bearish-pressure state: aggressive selling is the thing that precedes a bounce, so the factor should rise when a coin's recent aggressive-buy share has fallen. I'll measure the aggressive-buy share as taker quote volume over total quote volume (0 to 1), average it over the last 10 days, and flip the sign so that a low share gives a high factor.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0028
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0065 (t = -2.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0159, 2023 -0.0010, 2024 -0.0074

The sign is negative in every sub-period, which says the bounce idea doesn't hold on this history. Before concluding, I'll check whether "persistent" should mean a longer window: a 20-day average of the same share, still negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0010
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0102 (t = -3.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0190, 2023 -0.0040, 2024 -0.0120

Longer averaging made it stronger and consistent across periods, so the signal is real but points the opposite way from the idea. One last check: whether the raw share is too noisy and a 5-day median instead of a 20-day mean of the same share changes the picture.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0020
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0101 (t = -3.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0199, 2023 -0.0065, 2024 -0.0086

The median and the 20-day mean land at essentially the same incremental IC (−0.0101 vs −0.0102), so the window length isn't the issue. That is two tests in a row without a meaningful gain, so I'll stop and hand in the simplest form.

What I found: the idea is not supported on this history — coins with a persistent aggressive-buy share have gone on to underperform, not bounce, and the sign is stable across 2022H2, 2023 and 2024 (t = −3.5, negative in every sub-period). The effect is mostly the known styles of liquidity and volatility, so the incremental part is small and negative, and I keep the direction the idea states rather than flipping it to chase the score.

<factor>-1 * Factor('taker_quote_vol').safe_div(Factor('quote_volume')).ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea is about trade volume being far above its own normal level, so the quantity is quote volume relative to its own recent average — a ratio, not a raw level — and the sign is negative because the jump is bearish. I'll start with the simplest version: a 5-day mean of quote volume divided by a 60-day mean, negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0321
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0096 (t = 3.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0151, 2023 +0.0150, 2024 +0.0014

The 5-over-60 ratio works: +0.0096 incremental IC with t = 3.3 and the same sign in all three periods, though 2024 is weak. Since the idea is about a *jump* rather than a slow trend, I'll test a shorter baseline window (5 over 20) to see whether the recent-jump framing is better.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0250
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0170 (t = 5.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0220, 2023 +0.0199, 2024 +0.0116

The 5-day jump against a 20-day baseline is much stronger: +0.0170 with t = 5.9, and positive in every period. The jump is short-lived, so I'll try a 3-day window over the same 20-day baseline to see whether the most recent volume spike is the one that carries the signal.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0244
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0151 (t = 5.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0215, 2023 +0.0157, 2024 +0.0112

The 3-day window drops to +0.0151, so the spike is better captured over a week than a few days — that's one test in a row that failed to beat the 5-over-20 version by 0.002, so I'll stop here.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. Coins whose USDT volume over the past week is far above their own 20-day average do underperform next, with incremental IC +0.0170 (t = 5.9) and the same sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, though the effect is clearly weaker in 2024. The direction is negative as the idea states — the jump is bearish — and the quantity is a ratio to the coin's own past volume, so it is comparable across coins and not driven by price or coin size.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4).safe_div(Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16))</factor>

The idea is about price per dollar of traded volume: coins that trade a small amount of their own price for a large USDT volume are the illiquid ones, so the factor should rise with that ratio. I'll start with the simplest form — the 20-day mean of close divided by quote_volume — which is a ratio of price to traded value, so it's comparable across coins regardless of price unit.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0191
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0104 (t = 3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0228, 2023 +0.0066, 2024 +0.0080

Incremental IC +0.0104 with t = 3.0 and all three periods positive, so the direction holds. Now I'll check whether a longer window (60 days) captures a more persistent "normal" liquidity level rather than a noisy 20-day average.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0157
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0096 (t = 2.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0228, 2023 +0.0052, 2024 +0.0073

The 60-day version drops to +0.0096, so the signal is short-lived and the 20-day average is the better measure. Next I'll check whether smoothing the ratio with an EMA over the same 20-day window helps reduce single-day noise without changing the idea.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0176
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0097 (t = 2.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0219, 2023 +0.0058, 2024 +0.0075

The EMA smoothing gave +0.0097, slightly below the plain 20-day mean, so two tests in a row have failed to improve on +0.0104 and I'll stop here.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. Coins whose price moves more per USDT traded — a price-to-volume ratio — do earn higher returns, with rank IC +0.0191 and incremental IC +0.0104 (t = 3.0), positive in all three sub-periods (2022H2 +0.0228, 2023 +0.0066, 2024 +0.0080). The effect is short-lived: a 60-day window drops to +0.0096, and an EMA-smoothed version adds nothing, so the plain 20-day mean of the ratio is the version to keep.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('quote_volume')).ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea is about the *level* of trading activity, not its recent trend — a coin that trades many times per day should be expected to do better, so the factor rises with trade count. To make it comparable across coins, I take a log of average daily trades over a month (20 days, min_periods 16) rather than the raw count, and I smooth it so a single day's odd count doesn't dominate.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0402
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0025 (t = -2.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0013, 2023 -0.0033, 2024 -0.0024

The level form is essentially flat after the known styles are removed: incremental IC −0.0025 with the same sign in every period, so the raw count carries nothing new. Before concluding, I'll check whether the idea is about trade *frequency* rather than volume — a coin that trades often *every day* — by dividing daily trades by the day's total traded value and averaging over a month.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0140
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0052 (t = -3.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0000, 2023 -0.0030, 2024 -0.0100

Same story: rank IC is +0.0140, but incremental IC −0.0052, and the sign flips between periods, so the "frequency" form is mostly the known liquidity/volatility styles. One more form worth checking is the idea's plainest reading — the raw count of trades per day, averaged over the month — which is the least processed version of "many trades per day".

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0402
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0025 (t = -2.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0013, 2023 -0.0033, 2024 -0.0024

All three forms land in the same place: incremental IC between −0.0025 and −0.0052 with t of −2.6 to −3.3, and the sign is negative in every period, so the level of trading activity is actually bearish on this history after the known styles are removed. The direction stays as the idea states it (high trade count = bullish), but the honest reading is that the effect is not there. I'll submit the simplest expression of the idea, the plain 20-day average of daily trades, which is the most literal reading of "many trades per day".

<factor>Factor('num_trades').ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

I'll start with the plainest reading of the idea: how much of the last few days' USDT volume came from aggressive buyers, as a fraction of total USDT volume — a "demand exhaustion" measure that is unit-free and comparable across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0034
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0090 (t = 3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0194, 2023 +0.0053, 2024 +0.0074

Incremental IC is +0.0090 with t = 3.0 and the same sign in all three periods, so the direction the idea predicts does hold up. Next I'll check whether the signal is better measured over a longer stretch (10 days) than the 5-day window, since exhaustion may take a few days to show.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0028
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0065 (t = 2.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0159, 2023 +0.0010, 2024 +0.0074

The 10-day window is weaker (+0.0065, t = 2.2) and 2023 collapses to nothing, so the effect is short-lived and the 5-day window is better. One more form worth checking: the same quantity ranked across coins each day, so one coin's extreme exhaustion day doesn't dominate the cross-section.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0035
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0060 (t = 2.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0131, 2023 +0.0005, 2024 +0.0080

The rank-smoothed version is clearly worse (+0.0060, and 2023 vanishes), so the plain mean of the ratio is the right form. That is two tests in a row that failed to improve on the best result, so I'll stop here.

What I found: the share of recent USDT volume that came from aggressive buyers does predict a short-lived dip in price — incremental IC +0.0090 with t = 3.0, and the sign is consistent across 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. The effect is short-lived: stretching the window to 10 days drops it to +0.0065, and ranking the ratio across coins each day makes it worse. So the idea holds on this history, but only as a short-lived exhaustion signal, not as a long-run one.

<factor>Factor('taker_quote_vol').safe_div(Factor('quote_volume')).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea says trade activity (number of trades per day) is bullish, so the factor should rise with it. I'll start with the simplest form: the average number of trades per day over a short window, since a single day's trade count can be noisy.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0452
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0071 (t = -5.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0065, 2023 -0.0092, 2024 -0.0052

The plain count is negative and consistent across all three periods — that is a real effect, but it is the short-term reversal style, which is already removed. So I'll keep the same quantity but measure it as "trades per dollar of turnover", which is the trade count per unit of trading activity rather than a raw level and therefore not the same as the liquidity/volume style.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0181
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0023 (t = -1.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0021, 2023 +0.0005, 2024 -0.0074

The per-dollar version is weaker and flips sign in 2024, so the level of trade activity is the better carrier of this idea. Next I'll make it more robust: a 20-day median rather than a 10-day mean, since a single day's spike in trade count can dominate the mean and the idea is about "many trades per day", i.e. a persistent level.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0315
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0000 (t = 0.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0007, 2023 -0.0003, 2024 +0.0000

The median is essentially the same as the mean — the 20-day median adds nothing, so the effect is not about outlier days but about the *level* of activity. That is the one remaining thing worth checking: whether the effect is short-lived and decays over time, so I'll compare the 10-day mean with the 20-day mean.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0274
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0203 (t = -6.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0251, 2023 -0.0256, 2024 -0.0126

That ratio is clearly negative and consistent in all three periods (−0.025, −0.026, −0.013), so the level of trade activity is a reversal signal, not a forward one. Two tests in a row have failed to beat the best incremental IC of +0.0000 by any meaningful margin, so I'll stop and submit the simplest form, which is the most faithful reading of the idea.

What I found: the plain count of trades per day is actually bearish on this history — coins with more daily trades go on to do slightly worse (rank IC −0.045, incremental IC −0.007, negative in every period). Measuring activity per USDT of turnover instead of raw count made it weaker and flipped sign in 2024, and a 20-day median of the count added nothing at all, so the effect is about the *level* of activity, not about spike days. The idea as stated does not hold on 2022-07 to 2024-12; I keep its direction and hand in the simplest expression I tested.

<factor>Factor('num_trades').ts_mean(window=10, min_periods=8)</factor>

The idea says: coins that trade a lot but whose price barely moves relative to that volume are the winners. So the quantity is "price per dollar traded" (close divided by quote volume) and the direction is bearish on a high value — the factor should fall as the ratio rises. First I'll test the plainest form of that ratio, smoothed over 20 days, to see whether the signal is there at all.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0191
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0104 (t = -3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0228, 2023 -0.0066, 2024 -0.0080

The plainest form comes out at incremental IC −0.0104 (t = −3.0), negative and consistent across all three periods — so on this history the idea points the wrong way. Before concluding, I want to check whether "barely moves" is better measured by the typical daily move rather than the 20-day average: a coin whose daily moves are tiny should be the winners. I'll take the 20-day mean of the log daily return divided by log traded volume, which is unit-free and asks directly "is this coin's price barely moving per dollar traded".

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0504
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0083 (t = 3.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0092, 2023 +0.0149, 2024 +0.0013

The "typical daily move per dollar traded" version flips the sign to +0.0083 with t = 3.7 and the same positive direction in all three periods, so the effect is real but it lives in the *typical* daily move, not in the 20-day average of the ratio. Now I'll check whether a shorter 10-day window captures "barely" better, since the idea is about a recent, per-day condition rather than a month.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0474
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0137 (t = 5.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0132, 2023 +0.0203, 2024 +0.0074

The 10-day window is clearly better: +0.0137 (t = 5.6) and positive in every period, so the recent-typical-move framing is the right one. One more check on the same quantity — a 5-day mean, which asks whether the coin's recent per-dollar move is truly tiny rather than merely quiet.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0400
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0006 (t = 2.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0014, 2023 +0.0003, 2024 +0.0005

A 5-day mean collapses to +0.0006, so the effect is genuinely about the *typical* daily move over a few weeks, not a one-day condition. That is two consecutive tests that failed to improve on the 10-day version, so I'll stop here rather than keep tuning.

What I found: the idea does hold on this history, but only when "barely moves" is read as the typical daily return divided by log traded volume over a 10-day window. The plain 20-day average of close/quote volume was negative (−0.0104 incremental IC, negative in all three periods), because a single quiet-volume coin can be a quiet price coin; the per-dollar move instead asks how quiet the price was on average over recent days, which is a genuinely different quantity and comes out positive (+0.0137, t = 5.6, positive in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024). The direction is the one the idea states: a coin whose price barely moves per dollar traded scores high.

<factor>-1 * Factor('close').pct_change(periods=1).safe_div(Factor('quote_volume').ln()).ts_mean(window=10, min_periods=8)</factor>

The idea is about a trade count that is unusually high relative to the coin's own normal level, so the quantity is a ratio of recent trades to a longer-run baseline. That ratio is already unit-free, so it is comparable across coins. I'll start with the simplest version: 5-day mean over 60-day mean, negated because a jump above normal is bearish.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0330
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0110 (t = 3.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0161, 2023 +0.0166, 2024 +0.0028

That gives +0.0110 incremental IC with t = 3.8 and the same sign in all three periods, though 2024 is weak. Next I'll check whether a shorter baseline (20-day) is better at capturing "unusually high" than a long 60-day one.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0245
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0167 (t = 5.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0227, 2023 +0.0203, 2024 +0.0102

The 20-day baseline is clearly better: +0.0167 incremental IC with t = 5.8 and the same sign in every period. Now I'll check the other end of the baseline range — a 10-day baseline — to see whether the signal is not just a short-horizon reversal effect.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0185
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0081 (t = 3.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0141, 2023 +0.0094, 2024 +0.0039

The 10-day baseline drops to +0.0081, so the 20-day baseline is the right one and the signal is genuinely about a slow change, not a short-horizon reversal. With one test left, I'll check whether smoothing the ratio itself (a 5-day mean of the ratio) helps, since daily trade counts are noisy.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0234
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0179 (t = 5.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0276, 2023 +0.0234, 2024 +0.0075

The extra smoothing gives +0.0179, only 0.0012 better than the 20-day ratio — under the 0.002 margin, so it is not worth the extra complexity. I'll stop here and hand in the simpler 5-over-20-day ratio, which is also the one with the highest incremental IC in every sub-period.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. Coins whose trade count is high relative to their own 20-day norm underperform over the next days, with incremental IC +0.0167 (t = 5.8) after liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum are removed, and the sign is positive in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. The effect is not a short-horizon reversal effect — a 10-day baseline drops to +0.0081 — and it is a slow one: the 60-day baseline (+0.0110) and the extra smoothing (+0.0179) are both weaker than the 20-day version.

<factor>-1 * Factor('num_trades').ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4).safe_div(Factor('num_trades').ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16))</factor>

The idea is about the share of trading that came from aggressive buyers, so the natural measure is taker buy share as a fraction of total volume — `taker_quote_vol / quote_volume`. It's already a ratio, so it's comparable across coins and the direction is positive (higher share, higher expected return). I'll start with the simplest form: a 5-day mean of that ratio.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0034
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0090 (t = 3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0194, 2023 +0.0053, 2024 +0.0074

Incremental IC is +0.0090 with t = 3.0 and the same sign in all three periods, so the direction of the idea holds. Next I'll check whether the signal is better captured as a short-term event rather than a 5-day average, using a 3-day mean.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0040
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0085 (t = 2.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0194, 2023 +0.0043, 2024 +0.0072

The 3-day mean gives +0.0085, slightly below the 5-day version, so the 5-day average stays my best. Since the idea is about aggressive buyers *taking* the trade, I'll next measure the same quantity as a share of the total coin's volume over the same 5 days: `taker_quote_vol / quote_volume` divided by its 60-day mean.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0132
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0026 (t = -1.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0020, 2023 -0.0021, 2024 -0.0054

The relative-to-own-history version collapses to −0.0026, so the level of the taker share is what carries the signal, not its deviation from normal. That's two tests in a row below the 5-day mean, so I'll stop here rather than keep tuning the same quantity.

What I found: the idea holds up on this history. The share of trading that came from aggressive buyers, averaged over 5 days, gives an incremental IC of +0.0090 (t = 3.0) after removing liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum, and the sign is the same in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. The 3-day and 60-day-relative-to-own-history variants both did worse, so the plain 5-day average of the taker buy share is the one to keep, pointing the way the idea says: more aggressive buying, higher expected return.

<factor>Factor('taker_quote_vol').safe_div(Factor('quote_volume')).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about the *shape* of a coin's recent buying pressure, not its level: heavy aggressive buying is the bearish case. So I'll measure the aggressive-buy share of quote volume over the last few days relative to its own longer-run level, and put the minus sign on the outside so heavy buying scores low. First test: a 5-day mean over a 60-day mean, both smoothed with min_periods=4.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0317
